title: Dharma Just Locked Tiger Shroff, Janhvi Kapoor, and Lakshya Into a Revenge Love Story. Summer 2027 Has Its First Fight.
excerpt: Raj Mehta trades family comedies for fists, fury, and a 100-dancer showdown at Mukesh Mills — and Lakshya had to grow his hair back for it
body:
Karan Johar has always known how to make a date feel like an event. And when Dharma Productions locked May 14, 2027 for Lag Ja Gale, the message was unmistakable: clear your summer, this one's coming in hot.

The film brings together three of young Bollywood's most watchable faces — Tiger Shroff, Janhvi Kapoor, and Lakshya — in what's being described as a revenge-action love story. That's not a typo. Revenge. Action. Love story. All three genres in the same sentence, all directed by Raj Mehta, the man who made Good Newwz and JugJugg Jeeyo. If that pivot from family comedies to flying fists sounds dramatic, that's because it is. And it might be exactly the reinvention Raj Mehta needs.

Here's what we know so far: Tiger and Lakshya's characters are pitted against each other, while Janhvi's role weaves in the emotional core of the story. Think Ek Villain meets Kabir Singh meets something Dharma would actually put their money behind — polished, big-scale, and designed to fill every seat in every multiplex from Juhu to Jersey City.

The shoot kicked off in January 2026 in Mumbai and was originally slated to wrap by April. But then Lakshya had to step away for a few scenes of Chand Mera Dil, and the two films demanded completely different looks. He had to chop his hair, trade the rugged Lag Ja Gale avatar for something softer, and now he's growing it all back. The shoot won't wrap until October. Sometimes the most expensive thing on a film set is a haircut.

"While filming Lag Ja Gale, Lakshya had to shoot for a few scenes of Chand Mera Dil. His looks in both films are different. He had to not only cut his hair but also trade the rugged avatar of Lag Jaa Gale for the softer look." — Source to Mid-Day

But the detail that has the internet truly buzzing is a sequence shot at Mumbai's Mukesh Mills back in December 2025. Choreographed by Ganesh Acharya, it reportedly featured over 100 professional dancers in what's being described as a full-scale dance-off between Tiger and Lakshya. Tiger leaned into his signature athletic, gravity-defying style — the backflips, the speed, the sheer physical spectacle that's made him one of Bollywood's most distinctive movers. Lakshya, by contrast, went fluid and effortless, bringing the kind of easy charisma that's been quietly making him one of the industry's most interesting new faces.

This is the first time Tiger Shroff and Janhvi Kapoor have been paired on screen, and the pairing makes a certain kind of sense. Tiger brings the box office muscle and the action credentials. Janhvi, fresh off the polarising discourse around Peddi and its leaked chat controversy, gets to pivot into something that plays to her strengths — a large-scale commercial entertainer where the drama is baked into the story, not the social media cycle.

And then there's Lakshya, who's been building a quiet head of steam since his debut. He and Janhvi were originally supposed to share the screen in the now-shelved Dostana 2 — a project that became one of Bollywood's most talked-about cancellations. Lag Ja Gale finally gives them the frame together, and under circumstances that feel far more interesting than a Dostana sequel ever would have.

For the diaspora audience, the May 14 release date is strategic. It's deep into the summer holiday window — the sweet spot when NRI families hit theatres on the same day releases drop in Mumbai and Delhi. Dharma knows this corridor intimately. Their biggest commercial hits have historically been summer and holiday releases, and they're clearly positioning Lag Ja Gale as the tentpole.

Raj Mehta stepping into action territory is the wildcard here. His filmography has been built on charm, chemistry, and family dynamics — not fight choreography and revenge arcs. But if the Mukesh Mills dance-off is any indication, he's not just dipping a toe into the genre. He's diving in headfirst with 100 dancers and a swagger that says he's done being underestimated.

Summer 2027 just got its first must-watch. And Tiger Shroff, who's been searching for the right vehicle to reassert his theatrical dominance, might have found it in the most unexpected director's chair.
